bullets.text: Full-year CR 95.6 met 96.0 objective; post-tax underwriting profit $461M; net income $902M ($1.48/share); comprehensive EPS $1.78 (+23% YOY); comprehensive ROE 17.4%; Q4 CR reached 94.6.

Responded to 28 declared catastrophes in 2012 with highest ever catastrophe claim count; close to 1,300 people traveled to assist; company dedicated ~500,000 hours; 94% of Sandy claims resolved before year-end.
Written and earned premiums both cleared $16B; NPW grew 8% (+$1.23B YOY) to lead industry growth, compared to a five-year auto insurance industry CAGR rounding to zero.

Portfolio total return was 6.8% (nearly $700M post-tax); paid ~$600M ($1.00/share) dividend and declared $172M (over $0.28/share) variable dividend; repurchased 8.6M shares for ~$174M; pretax book yield was under 3%.

Unseasonably warm weather suppressed winter claim frequency, but claim severity rose faster than recent history; mid-year confirmed sustained severity increases, and quarterly underwriting results slipped to 97.6.

Rate revision infrastructure entered full response mode after quarterly results slipped; second-half advertising spend was reduced to align with profitability targets; the 96 combined ratio remains the central business model constant.
Snapshot UBI premiums topped $1B with multi-Mars-trip driving data; awarded 4th, 5th, and 6th UBI patents with licensing planned; acquired non-controlling equity interest in homeowners partner ASI.

Policies in force grew 3.7% in Personal Lines and 2.1% in Commercial Auto; one-year policy life expectancy fell 0.6% in personal auto and rose 0.3% in Commercial Auto; multi-product customers reached low teens.

Claims organization achieved lowest ever LAE run rate alongside strong resolution quality, with no decline in customer satisfaction; 54 concierge service centers operated, with several new co-located facilities planned.

Flo campaign expanded out-of-store, earning Ad Age Top Ten Female Ad Icon; 57% consumer awareness for Snapshot with 82% brand attribution; full-year advertising media and creative spend grew slightly.
